  - SMALL SLIDE 2 / BODY: Sources say Gottheimer "announced" the bills; Politico specifically says he "intends to introduce" them. "Introduced" implies formal legislative introduction, which the sources do not confirm. (SOURCES SAY: Press release: "announced a new bipartisan agenda"; WRNJ: "announced two bipartisan bills"; Politico/NewsBreak: "said Friday he intends to introduce two bipartisan bills")
  - SMALL SLIDE 4 / HEADLINE: The slide delivers only a number (30 days / one extension). It answers "how long," not "what the NSA would check." That content appears on slide 6 under a different headline. The headline overpromises what the slide delivers. (SOURCES SAY: Nothing about this headline framing; the 30-day figure is supported, but the headline misrepresents the slide's content.)
  - SMALL SLIDE 6 / BODY: Sources say "a serious cyberattack." Dropping "serious" removes a qualifier present in every source version of this description. (SOURCES SAY: Press release: "launch a serious cyberattack"; WRNJ: "conduct a serious cyberattack"; Politico: "launch a serious cyberattack")
  - SMALL SLIDE 9 / BODY: The sources don't state this fact. It is an inference drawn from Gottheimer's call on the Speaker to reconvene, not something any source says explicitly. (SOURCES SAY: Sources say Republican leadership has refused to bring the legislation to the floor and Gottheimer called on the Speaker to reconvene; no source states "a vote date has not been set.")
  - SMALL CAPTION / TEXT: Same error as slide 2. Sources say he "announced" the bills or "intends to introduce" them; formal introduction is not confirmed. (SOURCES SAY: Press release: "announced"; Politico/NewsBreak: "intends to introduce")
  - SMALL CAPTION / TEXT: "Steep climb" is editorial opinion not found in any source. Gottheimer said Republican leadership "refused to directly bring" the bills to a vote and called on the Speaker to reconvene, but no source characterizes the legislative prospects as a "steep climb." (SOURCES SAY: Gottheimer's remarks: "Republican leadership has refused to directly bring any of these critical pieces of legislation to the floor for a vote."
